catalysts: Valuation floor far above spot: the DCF's own bounds of $1352.63 (low) and $2028.94 (high) sit entirely above the $543.40 market price, with a mid-case $1690.79 — even the low end is roughly 2.5x the current quote, leaving substantial room for multiple re-rating toward the published band of $1268.09–$2113.48.

Growth differential as the re-rating trigger: the model fades revenue growth from 18.0% in FY1 to 3.0% in FY10 (10.5%/yr average), while the market at $543.40 implies -3.3%/yr flat for 10 years — below even the model's 3.0% terminal growth rate; any evidence that results track even a mid-single-digit trajectory compresses the implied 12.03% discount rate toward the model's 6.09% WACC.

Balance-sheet optionality funds the thesis: $7,220.1M of total assets against $819.8M of total liabilities and $6,400.3M of stockholders' equity at 2026-06-30, with a debt-free structure (the credit module reports no default barrier) — the DCF equity bridge adds net cash rather than subtracting net debt, so the $1352.63–$2028.94 range is not leveraged to a refinancing or rate event.

Insider-flow inflection would remove a supply overhang: 90-day net insider flow of -$280,134,185 with $0 of open-market purchases sets a low bar; a return of buying or the completion of the pre-arranged 10b5-1 option-exercise program (largest single sale $2,543,589) would eliminate the recurring Form 4 supply that has capped sentiment.

Momentum plus a severe implied discount: shares are +23.5% over one year and sit at the 67th percentile of the 52-week range, only -10.8% off the high, while the market-implied WACC of 12.03% (growth fade held fixed) looks punitive for an issuer printing FY2025 gross profit of $2,798.3M on FY2025 revenue of $3,182.7M (87.9%).
thesis.company_overview:
United Therapeutics Corporation is a public benefit corporation that commercializes therapies for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and other rare, life-threatening diseases, alongside an organ-manufacturing platform (ex-vivo lung perfusion and related technologies) intended to expand the supply of transplantable organs. The company sells branded, patent-protected therapies into a concentrated specialist-prescriber market, so revenue is driven by rare-disease patient volumes, label expansion and pricing rather than broad cyclical demand. TTM revenue was $3,154.5M with TTM net income of $1,310.9M; on an FY basis, FY2025 gross profit of $2,798.3M equalled 87.9% of FY2025 revenue of $3,182.7M, and FY2025 operating income of $1,492.5M equalled 46.9% of that revenue — a margin structure consistent with differentiated IP, not commodity generics.

A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. Geographic revenue breakdown was likewise not available from the supplied XBRL snapshot, so no geographic mix is cited here.

The balance sheet is debt-free — the structural credit model reports no barrier to breach — with $7,220.1M of total assets against $819.8M of total liabilities and $6,400.3M of stockholders' equity as of 2026-06-30. The durable moat rests on orphan-drug exclusivity and formulation/device IP in PAH, high switching costs within a specialist prescriber base, and manufacturing know-how in organ perfusion. Those assets, not balance-sheet leverage, are what must support the 18.0% FY1 growth rate, the 10.5%/yr average fade and the 3.0% terminal growth rate embedded in our valuation.
thesis.competitor_analysis: United Therapeutics competes in rare-disease specialty pharma, where the industry economics reward differentiated IP over manufacturing scale: FY2025 gross profit of $2,798.3M on FY2025 revenue of $3,182.7M (87.9%) and FY2025 operating income of $1,492.5M (46.9% of revenue) describe the margin structure of protected, concentrated prescriber markets rather than commodity generics, and a debt-free balance sheet ($7,220.1M of assets versus $819.8M of liabilities) means competitive defense is funded from internally generated cash rather than leverage. Because the peer-screen / peer-financials fetch returned no usable comp set for this run, no peer multiples are supplied and we make no premium-or-discount assertion against peers — the competitive read here is structural, resting on orphan exclusivity, device and formulation IP, and switching costs inside a specialist PAH prescriber base. On the evidence that does exist, the valuation conclusion rests on the DCF-versus-market comparison alone: a $1352.63–$2028.94 DCF band against a $543.40 spot price, with the market's own reverse-DCF implying a 12.03% discount rate or -3.3%/yr flat growth.

thesis.narrative:
We initiate coverage of United Therapeutics with a BUY, but with the point target withheld. The sole surviving method — a 10-year DCF on a 6.09% WACC, revenue growth fading from 18.0% in FY1 to 3.0% in FY10 (a 10.5%/yr average) and a 3.0% terminal growth rate applied after the window — outputs a mid-case $1690.79 inside a ±20% band of $1352.63–$2028.94, all of it above the $543.40 market price. The BUY reads off the nearest published range bound of $1268.09: the equity trades below the entire $1268.09–$2113.48 band, not merely below a midpoint.

The gap is a discount-rate story as much as a growth story. Holding the model's fade fixed, $543.40 implies a 12.03% WACC against the 6.09% the model uses — a 594 bp spread — and holding the WACC fixed, it implies -3.3%/yr revenue growth held flat for 10 years. Those are different constructs from the model's schedule, which declines rather than staying flat and averages 10.5%/yr; the market's flat -3.3% is below even the model's 3.0% terminal rate. That divergence, not a disagreement about the business, is why the verdict is directional and the confidence is very_low.

The operating base does not look like a melting ice cube: TTM revenue of $3,154.5M and TTM net income of $1,310.9M sit on FY2025 gross profit of $2,798.3M (87.9% of FY2025 revenue of $3,182.7M), with $7,220.1M of assets against $819.8M of liabilities and no debt. Offsetting that, insiders were net sellers to the tune of [target withheld] over the past 90 days with [target withheld] of open-market purchases, and the shares already carry +23.5% of one-year momentum at the 67th percentile of the 52-week range, -10.8% off the high.

Filed-event sentiment is neutral (net +0.00) across the SEC 8-K window, whose most recent entry is a 2026-09-08 material agreement under Item 1.01. Price action is constructive but not euphoric: +23.5% over one year, a 67% position within the 52-week range and -10.8% off the high. Net, the tape and the DCF-versus-market gap support the BUY direction, while the insider distribution pattern and the 12.03% market-implied discount rate justify withholding the point estimate at very_low confidence.

The earnings base is flattening against a reacceleration assumption: TTM revenue of $3,154.5M and TTM net income of $1,310.9M are already below FY2025's $3,182.7M and $1,334.7M, while the model's FY1 assumes 18.0% growth — a growth rate nearer the recent run-rate would cut the $1690.79 DCF mid materially and breach the $1352.63 low bound.

Terminal-value dependence: the model applies a 3.0% perpetuity growth rate only after the 10-year forecast window, so the conclusion rests on the terminal perpetuity, not the explicit forecasts; the market-implied -3.3%/yr flat 10-year rate (solved with the 6.09% WACC fixed) shows how quickly value erodes if the fade is steeper than modeled.

The valuation gap carries no second-method corroboration: only one method ran (DCF, weight 0.85, confidence very_low) and no peer comp set was produced for this run, so the $1268.09–$2113.48 band is unhedged by any cross-check — a single-model conclusion with a 3.1x gap to the $543.40 market price.
thesis.tagline: UTHR · BUY: DCF band above $543 spot; point target withheld
thesis.valuation_overview: Only one valuation method survived this run: a 10-year DCF on a 6.09% WACC, with revenue growth fading from 18.0% in FY1 to 3.0% in FY10 (a 10.5%/yr average across the forecast window) and a 3.0% terminal growth rate applied after it. That method produces a mid-case $1690.79 inside a ±20% band of $1352.63–$2028.94 (weight 0.85, confidence very_low). No peer-multiple comp set was produced for this ticker in this run — the peer screen / peer-financials fetch returned no usable comparables — so there is no second method and no weighted average to publish, and the lone surviving method sits 3.1x the $543.40 market price, outside the [0.5x, 2x] single-method calibration band used to sanity-check a single far-from-market output. The point target is withheld for exactly that reason: printing $1690.79 as a target would stamp false precision on one un-corroborated method. What we can publish is the ±25% confidence band of $1268.09–$2113.48, which sits wholly above spot, plus the reverse-DCF: the market implies a 12.03% discount rate with the fade fixed, or -3.3%/yr flat growth for 10 years with the WACC fixed — a flat rate, not the model's declining fade, and below even the 3.0% terminal rate.
